reply_text:
I've added a "memory as a service" section to the staging copy of index.html (futon7 `7d04b0c`). The live site is unchanged until you say so. The section sits just before "We can help you realise your vision", under your line as its heading:

> **We can remember it for you wholesale.**
>
> What we offer is memory: a custom memory system that your agents can use. Agents forget what they agreed, which questions are still open, and why the last decision was made, and people end up carrying that for them. We build a record of the work as it happens: what was asked, offered, promised and delivered, read from the conversation itself. Your agents consult it, and are reminded when something they owe has stalled. A working prototype runs our own agents every day (work-in-progress notebook). Each system has to be built around how your organisation actually works and what it already records, so it is a service we build with you rather than a product we ship.

It doesn't promise more than what runs today: the record of acts, the reminder machine, and the notebook link. It also keeps your point that the work is custom and hard.

For your sister, the one-line answer to "what vertical" is the opening of the paragraph: we build memory for teams that work with AI agents.

The page's preview description still says "Building the missing AI tools for software development." If memory is now the headline, that line could change to match. Shall I change it, and then put the index and 小象 page changes live?

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what changed)
- **Tangling.** 大象 proper, `futon3c.xiang.daxiang` (`read-agent-turn` and `asks-operator?`), is written in §2 of the notebook. `-m futon3c.notebook.render tangle notebooks/daxiang_live.clj` writes it to `src/futon3c/xiang/daxiang.clj`, which the JVM now loads. The token machine's "this turn ends by asking you" test now calls 大象, so there's one judge. 大象 also no longer counts a `🈸:` pointer (an answer to your 🈸) as a question.
- **Citations.** McCarthy's Elephant 2000 (Stanford 1992, revised 1998); Fong's *Causal Theories* (arXiv:1301.6201); *Decorated Cospans* (TAC 2015, arXiv:1502.00872). The page says mistakes in using them are ours. I left out the comb paper, because I couldn't verify its author.
- **Diagrams.** There are two, drawn as plain SVG (no layout engine is installed):
  - how intents flow from the turns through 小象 / 象 / 大象 into acts, the kernel, open ports, the reminder machine and futon1b;
  - the glued theory, coloured by which pattern owns each variable.
- **The cascade (§7–8).**
  - It's compiled from the library files: WR-26's `@why` cone, which is WR-26 → WR-8 and R20, then WR-8 → WR-0.
  - It uses one generic rule, taken from the library's own definition of `@why` ("a pattern's rationale is that it answers the problem this node states"). A pattern is unmet when its IF holds and its THEN doesn't. A problem counts as addressed when a pattern answering it holds.
  - It then runs on the real `象-off` switch from your log. The re-arm condition was written down ("Joe asks for 象 back") but isn't countable, so WR-26 and the cone above it come out unmet. A countable condition would have met all four.
  - The page states two cautions: other patterns outside this cone also answer those problems, and the countability test is only a first classical test.
